profiled_workloads.selection_reason: Lowest-speedup representative timing workload (speedup 0.389); 16-bit hot path at 4096x4096; primary target of the Coder's per-element-cost observation.
Dtype control for the same 4096x4096 shape (speedup 0.925); isolates byte/element effect from per-element ALU cost.
Second 16-bit dtype at the same shape; confirms the 16-bit regime is dtype-independent.
Largest fp16 case (1073741824 elements, 32768 programs); tests whether the 16-bit regime and per-program setup cost change at scale.
Largest fp32 case (1073741824 elements); the workload where this candidate already beats the reference, giving the memory-bound comparison point.

findings.label: Vector pipe dominates AI-vector-core time on every profiled size and dtype

evidence.unit: fraction of aiv_time; float16 [4096,4096]: aiv_time=249.4us, aiv_vec_time=179.3us, aiv_mte2_ratio=0.1163, aiv_mte3_ratio=0.0658, aiv_scalar_ratio=0.1215
fraction of aiv_time; float32 [4096,4096]: aiv_vec_time=158.4us, aiv_mte2_ratio=0.1911, aiv_mte3_ratio=0.0792, aiv_scalar_ratio=0.1171
fraction of aiv_time; float16 1073741824 elems: aiv_vec_time=10232.3us, aiv_mte2_ratio=0.1963, aiv_scalar_ratio=0.0705
fraction of aiv_time; float32 1073741824 elems: aiv_vec_time=9253.5us, aiv_mte2_ratio=0.2545, aiv_mte3_ratio=0.1031

evidence.value: MTE2 bandwidth utilization lower than 80% when active; MTE3 bandwidth utilization lower than 80% when active

findings.inference: The vector (AIV) pipe is the single busiest pipe in all five profiles (0.63-0.75 of aiv_time) and is 2.3-4.0x the combined MTE2+MTE3 DMA time. The vendor report independently flags both DMA pipes as under-utilized (<80% when active). This makes a vector-ALU bound, not a DMA/DRAM bound, the primary regime.

findings.label: Per-element vector throughput is ~93-116 Gelem/s and nearly dtype-independent
findings.inference: fp16, bf16 and fp32 all deliver ~90-116 Gelem/s through the vector pipe, varying with element width by only ~13-25%. If the limit were DRAM bytes the fp32 case would be ~2x slower per element than fp16; instead it is faster. This confirms the Coder's observation that the element cost is essentially a fixed per-element vector-ALU budget, not a per-byte memory cost.

findings.label: 16-bit inputs pay an extra on-chip fp32 upcast on the vector pipe (not extra UB DMA)

evidence.value: fp16 ~half of fp32, matching halved input bytes (2B vs 4B/element)
evidence.unit: us; fp32 47.5-48.1us vs fp16 28.8-29.0us (fp16 row in a28f5d241bbb4cfebf10e36b529af716/op_summary.csv)

findings.inference: The fp16/bf16 load traffic (MTE2) scales down with bytes as expected, so the fp32 upcast is NOT creating extra UB DMA traffic. Instead it appears as additional vector-pipe work: fp16/bf16 must issue element cast ops (fp16->fp32 on both operands, fp32->fp16 on the result) that fp32 does not, raising aiv_vec_time ~13-15% at the same element count. The 16-bit penalty is therefore on the vector pipe, compounding the already-dominant ALU cost.

findings.label: Effective DRAM throughput is halved on 16-bit dtypes; this is where the 2.5x loss to the reference comes from

evidence.metric: effective DRAM throughput (derived from avg_duration_us=13689.662 over 3 arrays x 2B x 1073741824 = 6.44GB)
evidence.unit: GB/s; float16 1073741824 elems; eval reference at 7.16ms is ~900 GB/s

evidence.metric: effective DRAM throughput (derived from avg_duration_us=14342.674 over 3 arrays x 4B x 1073741824 = 12.88GB)
evidence.unit: GB/s; float32 1073741824 elems; eval reference at 15.32ms is ~840 GB/s

findings.inference: The kernel reaches ~900 GB/s only in the fp32 large case, where bytes/element is high enough that the fixed vector-ALU work no longer hides DRAM. On fp16 the byte traffic halves but the vector work does not, so DRAM utilization collapses to ~472 GB/s (about half) and the speedup drops to 0.53. These large-case numbers are consistent with the Coder's read: the reference is memory-bound and bytes-proportional, ours is vector-work-bound and element-proportional.

findings.label: Per-program scalar/setup overhead is real but secondary (~6-12% of kernel time)

evidence.unit: fraction of aiv_time; float16 [4096,4096] grid=4096, UNROLL=1 vs large-case 0.0705 in workload-3ff0d451.../cc666e5dad954aeeaac91245af8a8ff7/op_summary.csv

findings.inference: Smaller tiles-per-program (the 4096-program case) show roughly double the scalar ratio and ~11% lower vector throughput than the 32768-program large case, so per-program setup/scalar cost exists and scales with grid size. But it accounts for at most ~12% of kernel time, so it cannot explain the 2.5x fp16 gap and is a secondary lever; the primary lever remains the per-element vector ALU budget.

performance_interpretation: The frozen experiment plan was a baseline-establishment plan with no bottleneck hypothesis to confirm or refute; the profiler evidence is consistent with, and quantifies, the Coder's post-hoc observation. Measured fact: the AI-vector (AIV) pipe carries 63-75% of kernel time on every profiled workload, while MTE2 (load) is 12-25%, MTE3 (store) 6.6-10%, and scalar 6-12%; the vendor summary independently reports both DMA pipes below 80% utilization when active. Per-element vector throughput is ~93-116 Gelem/s and nearly invariant across fp16/bf16/fp32, so the cost model is per-element ALU work, not per-byte DRAM. fp16/bf16 add further vector work for the fp32 upcast (vec_time +13-15% at identical element count) without extra UB DMA traffic. The consequence is exactly the observed speedup split: in the fp32 large case bytes/element are large enough that the kernel reaches ~905 GB/s and beats the reference (1.08x), whereas in 16-bit cases the halved byte traffic cannot hide the fixed vector work, DRAM utilization drops to ~472 GB/s (fp16 large) and speedup falls to 0.39-0.76. Inference (not measured): because the reference is memory-bound at ~850-900 GB/s while executing the same logaddexp2 math, the reference's element function must be much cheaper on the vector pipe than ours - most plausibly its exponential/logarithm lower to single hardware vector instructions, whereas tl.exp2/tl.log2 in this Triton/Ascend backend are suspected to expand to longer polynomial/intrinsic sequences. This could NOT be confirmed: the instruction-level (Ascend simulator) profile failed with 'profiling deadline expired during Ascend simulator kernel 0' for both requested workloads, so no instruction listing is available this round. The per-element vector instruction count of tl.exp2/tl.log2 and the split between transcendental cost, NaN-select cost, and cast cost remain unresolved and are the decisive open question for the next experiment.

next_experiment.action_description: Isolate and then cut the per-element vector-ALU budget of _lad2_elem. Step 1 (attribution): on the frozen snapshot, compile a small set of probe variants of the flat kernel that keep identical loads/stores/grid but change only the element function - (a) baseline, (b) transcendentals removed (drop tl.exp2/tl.log2, keep the m,d arithmetic), (c) NaN selects removed (drop the d!=d where and the nan OR/where), (d) casts removed (skip the .to(float32)/.to(element_ty) round trip) - and record aiv_vec_time / aiv_vec_ratio per variant on float16::2 and float32::2 plus float16::0. Step 2 (apply): implement the change indicated by the largest share - if (b) dominates, replace the tl.exp2/tl.log2 lowering with a cheaper path (a backend hardware vector exp/ln intrinsic, a libdevice fast variant, or a shared shorter polynomial); if (c) dominates, fold the two NaN tl.where selects into a single select; if (d) dominates, hoist the operand casts or compute the 16-bit path with fewer conversions. Keep the generic strided fallback and all 36 correctness cases untouched.
next_experiment.expected_impact: If the transcendentals dominate (expected, by analogy to the memory-bound reference), removing or cheapening them could cut aiv_vec_time by >50% and lift the 16-bit workloads from ~0.39-0.76 toward >1.0 speedup, moving headline geo_mean (currently 0.7927) materially; a smaller ~10-15% win is available from the cast/select reductions alone.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: The probe variants are additive and can be discarded without touching the committed path. Any change to NaN/inf handling risks breaking test_logaddexp2_non_finite (dtype0/1/2) and the inf-inf branches, and a cheaper transcendental approximation risks tolerance failures on the correctness shapes. Rollback is to the current solution_sha256 3d915c99...0f070e8 if vector time does not drop or any correctness case regresses.
success_criteria: All 36 correctness cases still pass, including test_logaddexp2_non_finite for float16/float32/bfloat16.
Headline geo_mean improves above the current 0.7927.
The fp16 4096x4096 workload's speedup rises above 0.39 (ideally >1.0) and its aiv_vec_ratio / aiv_vec_time drops relative to this round's 0.719 / 179.3us.
No regression on the already-winning float32 large case (must stay >1.0).

warnings: The instruction-level profile (level=instruction) failed for both requested workloads with 'profiling deadline expired during Ascend simulator kernel 0'; no instruction listing / Ascend instruction counts were produced, so the tl.exp2/tl.log2 expansion and load/store vector width questions could not be answered directly.
msprof timings (aiv_time, aiv_vec_time, pipeline ratios) are diagnostic and are not eval latency; all speedup/latency numbers in this analysis are taken from get_profile_context.

The vendor report tarballs (msprof-report.tar.gz / msprof-op-report.tar.gz) could not be unpacked in this environment, so only the CSV summary, base-collection logs, and the partial op-kernel log were read.
open_questions: How many vector instructions do tl.exp2 and tl.log2 expand to on this flagtree/Ascend backend - single hardware vexp/vln instructions or multi-term polynomial sequences?

Are the loads/stores 128/256-bit vectorized, and does the fp16/bf16 upcast appear as extra vector cast instructions rather than UB traffic? Metrics suggest yes for the vector-pipe cost, but no instruction/byte counters were obtained.
Can the two NaN tl.where selects and the fp32 round-trip be removed or fused without failing the non_finite correctness cases?
